title: Archangel Michael's Lenten Season: tradition and protection rituals
seoTitle: Archangel Michael's Lenten Season: traditions & protection
subtitle: 40 days of prayer that trace back to Saint Francis of Assisi and bring protection rituals
excerpt: From Aug 15 to Sep 29 the Church marks Saint Michael’s Lenten season, a 40‑day stretch of fasting, prayer and rituals that boost spiritual protection.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Beginning on August 15, the Lenten season of Archangel Michael returns to mark the Brazilian Catholic calendar, bringing 40 days of prayer, fasting and spiritual protection practices.

The tradition of Michael’s Lenten season

According to Father André de Moraes, pastor of the Catholic Community "Mar a Dentro", the practice dates back to 1224, when Saint Francis of Assisi performed his first Lenten season on Mount Alverne, dedicating it to God, the Virgin Mary and Archangel Michael. The period, which runs until September 29, coincides with the celebration of the archangels Michael, Gabriel and Raphael.

Spiritual meaning of fasting and vigilance

The priest explains that the desert symbolizes the sole presence of God, where “there is nothing, only God, and there God is enough.” Fasting and vigils, especially in the early morning hours, reinforce discipline, trust and spiritual vigilance, preparing the faithful to face the “modern storms” of life.

Recommended protection rituals

  • Light a white candle: the candle should remain lit daily, accompanied by a clear intention of personal, family or professional protection. As tarot reader Isabel Fogaça states, “the candle works as a focal point for intention.”
  • Indigo bath: indigo, a blue color associated with the archangel, is diluted in water and applied from the neck downwards. The specialist emphasizes that “blue is the frequency of Archangel Michael” and that the bath symbolizes “wearing protection.”
  • Smudging with rue: the herb is burned and the smoke circulates through all rooms, with doors and windows open so dense energies can exit. Fogaça notes that “the smudging breaks this charge and renews the environment.”

The early‑morning rosary as a highlight

One of the standout moments of the Lenten season is the Early‑Morning Rosary, practiced in the first hours of the day. The priest emphasizes that this practice “creates a profound impact on the life of those who practice it” and reinforces the idea that God becomes a priority.

Why the Lenten season is gaining prominence now

In recent years, the devotion has attracted a growing number of faithful, who see Michael’s Lenten season as an opportunity to reinforce spiritual protection in the face of personal and collective challenges. The blend of Franciscan tradition, simple rituals, and belief in the archangel’s intercession creates an atmosphere of hope and renewal for practitioners.

With information from News – Canção Nova, Terra.
